materiality: DeepSeek-V4.1 FlashInfer DSpark non-causal sparse attention needs visible-window metadata that excludes padded sparse slots and remains correct across graph replay.
The upstream repair adds direct reference comparisons across context lengths, BF16/FP8 and CUDA graph replay, so prior DeepSeek-V4.1 or FlashInfer receipts cannot be inherited.
requiredEvidence: Bind exact vLLM source/image, DeepSeek-V4.1 model/config, FlashInfer version, DSpark configuration, SM capability and dtype.
Run the known-bad predecessor and candidate against an independent dense/reference oracle for causal and non-causal sparse windows across short, boundary and long contexts.
Exercise BF16 and FP8, multiple head counts, padded decode slots, CUDA graph capture/replay and changing Q/KV/visibility without recapture; require output parity within declared tolerances.
Preserve incumbent serving rollback; missing SM100/required runtime is UNAVAILABLE, not PASS.

materiality: GLM-5.3-Flash could fail during ROCm AITER sparse-MLA initialization because ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl lacked the logical-topk readiness hook expected by the shared sparse-attention interface.

The repair intentionally supplies a no-op hook because this implementation shares the top-k indices buffer but does not participate in sparse-MLA index groups; that lifecycle assumption must be measured, not inferred.
requiredEvidence: Bind exact vLLM source/image, GLM-5.3-Flash artifact, ROCm/AITER versions, accelerator and sparse-attention configuration.
Reproduce the predecessor boot/initialization failure on the affected path and prove the candidate reaches ready state without bypassing another admission check.

Exercise repeated initialization, warm restart, worker restart and representative prompt/decode traffic while asserting the shared top-k buffer lifecycle and absence of stale index-group synchronization.
Keep unsupported hardware/runtime UNAVAILABLE and preserve rollback to the incumbent qualified backend.

materiality: MXFP8 MoE backend selection on ROCm must respect the actual AITER fused-MoE enable state rather than treating package/device presence as sufficient admission.
Selecting an AITER path while its runtime gate is disabled is a backend-contract violation, not a routine performance choice.
requiredEvidence: Bind exact vLLM source/image, ROCm/AITER/FlyDSL versions, gfx target, model quantization metadata and TP/EP topology.
Use AITER-enabled and AITER-disabled controls for both auto-selection and explicit backend requests; disabled state must never silently select AITER.
Compare candidate output/logits against the qualified native fallback on representative MXFP8 MoE inputs and exercise TP plus EP expert-mask paths.
Require explicit failure for unsupported forced selection, record rollback, and keep unexecuted gfx/topology combinations UNQUALIFIED.

materiality: DiffusionGemma could hand out stashed logprobs for a request that merely had decode logits rather than for the request that was actually committing its step.
Mis-associating pending logprobs across diffusion commit state is an output-integrity defect that can corrupt downstream scoring/evaluation evidence.
requiredEvidence: Bind exact vLLM source/image, DiffusionGemma model/config, sampler/logprob settings and request identities.
Reproduce the predecessor with mixed committing and non-committing requests, then require the candidate to pop and attach pending logprobs only for committing slots.
Exercise multi-request batching, slot reuse, logprobs enabled/disabled, cancellation before commit, retry/restart and repeated diffusion steps; assert no stale logprob crosses request identity.
Bind emitted token/logprob receipts to the exact request/commit step and preserve rollback; no evaluation score may be promoted from ambiguous predecessor output.

materiality: On ROCm AITER, requesting DeepSeek-V4 FP4-to-FP8 dequantization could be silently ignored because the native FP4 expert path returned before the dequant branch.
The repair converts routed expert weights/scales, normalizes e4m3fn to native FNUZ where required and avoids AITER shuffling for a Triton runner; wrong-runner shuffling can corrupt output.
requiredEvidence: Bind exact SGLang source/image, DeepSeek-V4 checkpoint identity, ROCm/AITER versions, accelerator, dequant environment and selected MoE runner.
Known-bad predecessor must show the requested dequant path is a no-op; candidate must prove FP4 expert weights/scales become the intended block-FP8 representation.
Exercise FNUZ and non-FNUZ hardware paths plus AITER and Triton runners; assert shuffle occurs only for the compatible AITER runner and compare logits to a trusted reference.
Record memory/performance only after numerical parity; preserve native FP4 rollback and mark absent hardware UNAVAILABLE.

materiality: SGLang now exposes opt-in runtime switching between prefill and decode roles, including transfer-backend teardown and lifecycle reconstruction rather than a restart-only topology change.

The source explicitly rejects DP attention, EP, MoE all-to-all, PP, DP, DCP and speculative decoding because role-specific state is not rebuilt for those combinations; promotion therefore requires lifecycle evidence, not feature discovery.
requiredEvidence: Bind exact SGLang source/image, transfer backend, network/bootstrap configuration, model, accelerator topology and role-switch flag; keep the flag off by default.

Run repeated P->D->P cycles with quiescent and in-flight workloads; prove request drain/cancellation, heartbeat thread shutdown, transfer-resource teardown/recreation and KV ownership without leak or duplication.
Inject teardown, registration, transfer and restart failures; require deterministic recovery or fail-closed service state with no mixed-role acceptance.
Assert every source-declared unsupported combination hard-fails before service admission; no success on the supported subset may qualify DP/EP/PP/DCP/speculative combinations.

alignmentDependency.note: Fresh HF runtime and a-11-oy.com reads still report the protected A11oy SHA; a11oy.net proof remains dated. Different observation windows are not combined into a whole-chain PASS.
